points.title: 早年求学
points.description: 乔纳斯·索尔克1914年出生于纽约市一个犹太移民家庭。他在纽约市公立学校接受基础教育，展现出对科学的浓厚兴趣。1929年，15岁的索尔克进入纽约市立学院，主修化学。这段时期，他受到导师托马斯·弗朗西斯的影响，对医学研究产生了浓厚兴趣，为他后来从事病毒学研究奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Jonas Salk was born in 1914 in New York City to Jewish immigrant parents. He received his primary education in New York City public schools, showing an early interest in science. In 1929, at age 15, Salk entered City College of New York, majoring in chemistry. During this period, he was influenced by his mentor Thomas Francis, who sparked his interest in medical research, laying the foundation for his later work in virology.

points.title: 医学研究起步
points.description: 索尔克进入纽约大学医学院学习，1939年获得医学学位。在医学院期间，他师从病毒学家托马斯·弗朗西斯，专注于流感病毒研究。毕业后，他成为弗朗西斯的助理，参与美国陆军传染病研究项目。这段经历使索尔克掌握了病毒培养和疫苗研发的基本技术，为他后来开发脊髓灰质炎疫苗积累了宝贵经验。
points.descriptionEn: Salk attended New York University School of Medicine, earning his medical degree in 1939. During his medical studies, he worked under virologist Thomas Francis, focusing on influenza virus research. After graduation, he became Francis's assistant and participated in the U.S. Army's infectious disease research program. This experience equipped Salk with essential techniques in virus cultivation and vaccine development, providing him with valuable expertise for his later work on the polio vaccine.

points.title: 脊髓灰质炎疫苗研发
points.description: 1947年，索尔克成为匹兹堡大学病毒研究部的负责人。在这里，他开始了脊髓灰质炎疫苗的研发工作。索尔克采用灭活病毒技术，通过化学方法杀死病毒但保留其免疫原性。经过多年的实验室研究和临床试验，1955年4月12日，索尔克宣布其疫苗安全有效，这一消息震惊了世界。他的疫苗迅速大规模生产，使美国脊髓灰质炎发病率在几年内下降了90%以上，挽救了无数生命。
points.descriptionEn: In 1947, Salk became the head of the Virus Research Laboratory at the University of Pittsburgh. Here, he began his work on developing a polio vaccine. Salk employed the killed virus technique, using chemical methods to inactivate the virus while preserving its immunogenic properties. After years of laboratory research and clinical trials, on April 12, 1955, Salk announced that his vaccine was safe and effective, news that stunned the world. His vaccine was rapidly mass-produced, reducing polio incidence in the United States by over 90% within a few years, saving countless lives.

points.title: 科研转型
points.description: 1960年，索尔克移居加利福尼亚州拉霍亚，创立索尔克生物研究所并担任首任所长。在这里，他将研究重点从疫苗开发转向基础生物学研究，探索生命的本质和免疫系统的奥秘。索尔克对多发性硬化症、阿尔茨海默症等神经系统疾病进行了深入研究，并提出了'免疫治疗'概念。他还积极参与科学伦理讨论，关注科学与社会的关系，成为科学界的人文主义倡导者。
points.descriptionEn: In 1960, Salk moved to La Jolla, California, where he founded the Salk Institute for Biological Studies and served as its first director. Here, he shifted his research focus from vaccine development to fundamental biology, exploring the nature of life and the mysteries of the immune system. Salk conducted in-depth research on neurological disorders such as multiple sclerosis and Alzheimer's disease, and proposed the concept of 'immunotherapy.' He also actively participated in discussions on scientific ethics, focusing on the relationship between science and society, becoming a humanist advocate in the scientific community.

points.title: 晚年贡献
points.description: 在生命的最后二十年，索尔克继续担任索尔克研究所所长，同时将更多精力投入到科学哲学和人类未来研究中。他提出了'人类进化新方向'理论，探索人类如何通过科学和道德进步实现自我超越。索尔克还积极参与全球健康政策讨论，关注人口增长、环境变化等全球性问题。1995年6月23日，索尔克在拉霍亚逝世，享年80岁。他的遗产不仅包括脊髓灰质炎疫苗这一伟大成就，还包括对科学与社会关系的深刻思考，以及对人类未来的乐观展望。
points.descriptionEn: In the last two decades of his life, Salk continued to serve as director of the Salk Institute while devoting more energy to scientific philosophy and research on humanity's future. He proposed theories on 'new directions in human evolution,' exploring how humanity could achieve self-transcendence through scientific and moral progress. Salk also actively participated in discussions on global health policy, addressing global issues such as population growth and environmental change. On June 23, 1995, Salk died in La Jolla at the age of 80. His legacy includes not only the monumental achievement of the polio vaccine but also profound reflections on the relationship between science and society, and an optimistic outlook for humanity's future.

appraisal.zh: 索尔克被普遍视为20世纪最伟大的医学英雄之一，他的脊髓灰质炎疫苗拯救了数以百万计的生命，拒绝为疫苗申请专利、将其视为献给人类的礼物更被传为科学道德的典范，他创立的索尔克研究所也成为顶尖的生物医学研究中心。不过也有研究者指出，其灭活疫苗路线后来被减毒活疫苗取代，他在推广中过于自信而忽视潜在风险，且过度个人化了战胜脊髓灰质炎的功绩，淡化了萨宾等人的贡献。
appraisal.en: Salk is widely regarded as one of the greatest medical heroes of the 20th century: his polio vaccine saved millions of lives, his refusal to patent it and his description of it as a gift to humanity became a byword for scientific integrity, and the Salk Institute he founded grew into a leading biomedical research center. Yet some researchers note that his inactivated-vaccine approach was later superseded by attenuated live vaccine, that his confidence in promoting the vaccine overlooked potential risks, and that he personalized the victory over polio, overshadowing contributions such as Sabin's.

supporter.zh: 乔纳斯·索尔克被视为20世纪最伟大的医学英雄之一。他的脊髓灰质炎疫苗拯救了数百万人的生命，改变了全球公共卫生格局。索尔克的无私精神——拒绝为疫苗申请专利，将其作为'人类的礼物'——体现了科学家的崇高道德。他创立的索尔克研究所成为世界顶尖的生物医学研究中心，培养了无数杰出科学家。索尔克不仅是一位医学创新者，更是一位科学人文主义者，他的工作超越了单纯的医学成就，对人类未来和科学伦理的思考至今仍有深远影响。
supporter.en: Jonas Salk is regarded as one of the greatest medical heroes of the 20th century. His polio vaccine saved millions of lives and transformed global public health. Salk's selfless spirit—refusing to patent the vaccine, presenting it as 'a gift to humanity'—embodies the highest moral principles of a scientist. The Salk Institute he founded has become a world-leading biomedical research center, nurturing countless outstanding scientists. Salk was not only a medical innovator but also a scientific humanist whose work transcended mere medical achievements, with his thoughts on humanity's future and scientific ethics continuing to have profound influence today.

critic.zh: 批评者指出索尔克的疫苗研发方法存在争议，他的'灭活疫苗'技术后来被更先进的'减毒活疫苗'所取代，后者提供了更持久的免疫保护。此外，索尔克在疫苗推广过程中过于自信，忽视了潜在风险，导致一些不良反应事件。还有人批评索尔克过度个人化脊髓灰质炎的战胜，忽视了阿尔伯特·萨宾等其他科学家的贡献。在科学方法论上，索尔克有时被视为'应用型'而非'理论型'科学家，其基础科学研究的影响力不及他的疫苗成就。
critic.en: Critics point out that Salk's vaccine development approach was controversial, as his 'inactivated vaccine' technology was later replaced by the more advanced 'attenuated live vaccine,' which provided longer-lasting immunity. Additionally, Salk was overly confident in the vaccine's promotion, overlooking potential risks, which led to some adverse reaction incidents. Others criticize Salk for overly personalizing the victory over polio, downplaying the contributions of other scientists like Albert Sabin. In terms of scientific methodology, Salk is sometimes viewed as an 'applied' rather than 'theoretical' scientist, with his basic scientific research having less impact than his vaccine achievements.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，乔纳斯·索尔克被定义为'疫苗革命'的象征人物，代表了科学进步如何能够解决重大公共卫生危机。他的故事成为科学英雄主义的经典案例，被广泛传播于书籍、纪录片和流行文化中。索尔克的形象超越了单纯的科学家，成为人类战胜疾病的象征。然而，历史学界也日益认识到，脊髓灰质炎的战胜是集体努力的成果，包括政府支持、公众参与和国际合作。索尔克的遗产提醒我们，科学进步不仅需要技术创新，还需要伦理考量和社会责任。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Jonas Salk is defined as a symbolic figure of the 'vaccine revolution,' representing how scientific progress can address major public health crises. His story has become a classic case of scientific heroism, widely disseminated in books, documentaries, and popular culture. Salk's image transcends that of a mere scientist, becoming a symbol of humanity's victory over disease. However, historians increasingly recognize that the conquest of polio was a collective achievement, involving government support, public participation, and international cooperation. Salk's legacy reminds us that scientific progress requires not only technological innovation but also ethical considerations and social responsibility.

self.zh: 我希望人们记住我是因为我给了他们一种选择，而不是因为我剥夺了他们的选择。
self.en: I hope that people will remember me because I gave them something, and because I was something.
